Mina Patel: quick heads-up — during SOC prep we discovered audit coverage gaps across billing write flows and runtime model load/eval actions. broken down by service: api-gateway, auth, console, billing, runtime.
Sam Ortiz: can you paste the specific missing events?
Mina Patel: billing: invoice export, manual credit adjustments, billing-API webhook deliveries (success/fail) missing customer-visible audit events. runtime: model hot-reload, model-variant-fallback, cache-eviction events missing. auth/console: role grants are emitted but no before/after role snapshot.
Devon Lee: that lines up with the QA trace I looked at — we have request_id in raw logs but schema doesn't normalize actor_id/org_id consistently.
Alisha Nguyen: important for customers who need proof of changes and for compliance. We should treat billing exports + role_changes as high priority for customer-facing validation. :exclamation:
Ryan Chen: KMS question: do we need to log key_id for envelope encryption used when we ship audit blobs to customers? is logging the key_id considered sensitive?
Julia Park: logging key_id is fine; we must not log any key material. also log kms_operation (Encrypt|Decrypt) and keyring type (aws-kms/gcp-kms/hsm) for traceability.
Mina Patel: agreed. for customer-facing audit events we should include key metadata but mask ops. propose schema fields: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_display, actor_ip, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, trace_id, org_id, client_version, key_id (nullable), kms_provider, and redaction_flags.
Sam Ortiz: +1. also add `before`/`after` for mutating ops but limit to small diffs. DO NOT include PII in before/after. we need guidance for the console team on redaction rules.
Devon Lee: implementation note — runtime emits a lot of high-cardinality fields. we should avoid putting full model weights/hash in events. only model_id, model_tag, and commit_sha (short) are OK.
Alisha Nguyen: for billing export events, customers asked to be able to validate that the export happened and which S3 bucket/object was used. we can include s3_object but redact presigned urls and tokens.
Mina Patel: backlog triage proposal: split into 5 workitems: RW-SEC-1452 schema v2 audit spec, RW-GW-259 gateway audit adapters, RW-AUTH-503 role-change normalization, RW-BILL-177 billing export audit, RW-RUNTIME-311 model-load audit. owners: sam=gateway, alisha=billing, devon=console/auth, ryan=runtime, mina=spec owner. timeline: 3 sprints for full coverage, quick wins (role_change before/after + key_id) in 1 sprint.
Sam Ortiz: I'll pick up RW-GW-259 and the adapter; will prototype a normalized JSON envelope for gateway events.
Ryan Chen: I'll do RW-RUNTIME-311 — first PR will add model-load and variant-fallback events with low-cardinality fields.
Devon Lee: I'll drive RW-AUTH-503 with help from console eng; propose default redaction policy: redact any field matching email, ssn, phone, token, api_key. we should publish a short doc for customers.
Alisha Nguyen: I'll own RW-BILL-177 and coordinate with storage/compliance on S3 proofs + KMS metadata.
Mina Patel: excellent. next steps: 1) I will open RW-SEC-1452 with the spec + example events + migration notes. 2) owners open PRs against their services and tag `sec-audit` and `compliance-review`. 3) set up automated validation: CI check that events conform to schema and that examples pass redaction tests.
Julia Park: sec-bot reminder: please link any PRs to RW-SEC-1452 so we can track coverage.
sec-bot: New issue created: RW-SEC-1452 — "Audit schema v2 + customer-facing validation" (https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RW-SEC-1452)
Sam Ortiz: quick question on validation: should CI fail builds that remove required audit fields, or only warn? we might break things.
Mina Patel: initial enforcement: warn + dashboard alerts for 2 weeks, then hard fail on missing required fields for any merge to main. owners can request exemptions with documented justification.
Devon Lee: can we add a lightweight local validator? maybe a node script `tools/audit-validate.js` that teams can run pre-commit.
Mina Patel: yes, add to spec. include example payloads and a small lib in `redwood-infra` so teams can reuse.
Alisha Nguyen: customer-facing validation note: we need to produce a mapping doc that explains which event types are available to customers and what fields are guaranteed. I'll draft an initial FAQ once RW-BILL-177 has the schema.
Ryan Chen: will add metrics: percent of requests with validated audit event + per-service coverage. we can surface that in Console and in the compliance export.
Mina Patel: thank you. I'll create the RW-SEC-1452 ticket now and assign owners. tagging follow-ups in threading: @Sam Ortiz @Alisha Nguyen @Devon Lee @Ryan Chen @Julia Park. :eyes:
Sam Ortiz: thanks — will sync after lunch and push a prototype envelope.
Devon Lee: noted. I'll assemble the redaction checklist and link it to the ticket.
Alisha Nguyen: adding product compliance review slot next Wed 10am.
Julia Park: adding a brief note for CS so they can field customer questions about scope.
Mina Patel: logging action items in the ticket. closing for now — please update RW-SEC-1452 with PR links and status. :white_check_mark:
